goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
goldens.reasoning: G1 is about float:left mixed with flexbox and losing the right alignment of the .d-header .panel login panel in the noscript header. C1 is about .small-action-desc shrinking inside a flex container in topic-post.scss. Both involve floats inside flex layouts, but they point to different code and different problems.

goldens.comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate mentions the invalid -ms-align-items prefix.

goldens.comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate mentions that box-ordinal-group values must start at 1.

candidates: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:264 - Making `.small-action` a flex container shrinks `.small-action-desc` to its content, so right-floated buttons no longer reach the right edge.. Before this change, `.small-action-desc` was an ordinary block that took the full row width. Its buttons (`button { float: right; }`) sat at the far right of the post. With `.small-action` now `display: flex`, `.small-action-desc` becomes a flex item with no `flex-grow`, so it is only as wide as its content. For a short action like "closed this topic", the delete/edit buttons now float right inside that narrow box, next to the text instead of at the edge of the post. If any button is a direct child of `.small-action`, its float is ignored entirely, because floats have no effect on flex items. I could not see the template, so I can't tell which of the two applies. Fix: add `flex: 1 1 auto;` (or `flex-grow: 1`) to `.small-action-desc` so it fills the remaining space as it did before.
